A_general.open_code_note: The official repository packages the hosted endpoint registration and client-specific plugin metadata and skills. Its README identifies https://mcp.zoominfo.com/mcp as the hosted server. It contains no server implementation or tool schemas, so it is not the deployed server code.
A_general.implementation_language: NOT FOUND (the repository contains plugin metadata, Markdown skills, and a JavaScript validation script, not server implementation)
other_official_servers: The documentation describes user-level OAuth and app-level Client Credentials authentication to the same MCP endpoint, not separate server endpoints: https://gtm.ai/guides/oauth-vs-client-credentials-zoominfo-mcp.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MCP platform access is included at no extra cost. Free signup includes 1,000 data credits and 1,000 AI credits. The pricing page lists data credits at $0.38 each at the $1,000 spend tier and AI credits at $0.05 each; top-ups start at $20. Pricing page also advertises a limited 70% discount on a first data-credit purchase.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free account available; Enterprise pricing is custom. The official pricing page lists Free and Enterprise tiers.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Data credits fund enrichment and record ingestion; AI credits fund research and analysis. The pricing page advertises 1,000 signup credits of each type. It also lists no extra MCP platform fee, standard API limits, and credit top-ups. Credits are shared across MCP, API, CLI, and web app. Pricing describes its own credit terms; the credits documentation notes that older subscriptions with only recurring monthly credits cannot be used by MCP.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires ZoomInfo login or app authentication and applicable package entitlements. Admin-only seats and accounts with only recurring monthly credits cannot use MCP. User-level results follow that user's entitlements; client-credentials calls use the integration user's identity. Per-user data and AI credit limits can be set by an admin. Pricing page lists 5 requests/second and 5 apps for the free tier.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization admin; client operators choose the OAuth flow and clients may disable individual tools.

An official plugin repository distributes client-side GTM workflow skills alongside the hosted endpoint registration. The tools reference says new tools are available at the next session start. The endpoint uses Streamable HTTP per client setup docs.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The tools reference identifies search, lookup, browse, and research actions as read-oriented and audience/context writes as write actions; no MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented. The credits page says the starter prompt asks the AI to estimate costs and check with the user before paid research; this is client guidance. Upsert Audience has structured fields that override conflicting agentInstruction text. 3. OAuth metadata lists scopes [openid, profile, zi_api, email, offline_access, zi_mcp, api:data:mcp]. Docs say calls use the signed-in user's entitlements; Client Credentials uses one integration identity and its permissions. Admins can cap per-user credits. Registration/redirect approval and token lifetime are not specified. 4. No documented read-only endpoint, toolset filter, or URL/header restriction mode found. Clients can enable/disable tools; user-sign-in and Client Credentials are documented modes. 5. Docs state package entitlements bound accessible data and fields; connected CRM/conversation sources and user permissions bound context. No field masking or PII exclusion policy specific to MCP found. 6. Credits: enrich Companies/Contacts up to 10 records per call; signals up to 10 companies; Manage Audience Rows up to 50 records per call; Browse Engagements up to 50 items and 90-day span. Data credits charge per new record/signal; AI research costs vary by work. Credit limits can be set per user. 7. Public server code and MCP input schemas unavailable. Docs state immutable audience type/searchQuery and column dataType values are silently ignored on updates; structured fields supersede conflicting agentInstruction. 8. ZoomInfo processes tool parameters and results; docs say it cannot see the rest of the AI conversation and server keeps no chat history between calls. Audit logging, telemetry, and opt-out are not documented. 9. FAQ names Submit Feedback; submitted requests feed directly into the tool roadmap. No vendor upsell response or tool-selection instruction is documented. 10. Server-provided initialize instructions not available. Official repository distributes external client skills; these guide task workflows but are not proven server-enforced. Docs contain tool-selection recommendations, including describing a task in natural language and asking before paid research. 11. Docs state the server retains no chat history between calls; user/context sources affect individual results. No learned agent behavior or persistent MCP memory documented. 12. Context/research tools use sub-agents to gather/synthesize connected data; this is tool-internal agent processing. The server otherwise presents a flat documented tool list and shared endpoint. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary execution tool found in the official active tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: “You rarely need to name a tool. Describe what you want and your AI client picks the right ZoomInfo tool, or chains several: building a list usually runs Lookup → Search → Enrich.”
“New tools published by ZoomInfo are available automatically at the start of each new session.”
“If the instruction text conflicts with a structured field like name or type, the structured field wins.”
“The starter prompt asks your AI to estimate credits and check with you before it runs paid research, and you can ask for the same in any prompt.”

“If the tool call comes back "No approval received" or a similar permission response, say so plainly, name the tool, and continue with the remaining steps. Don't retry the same call hoping for a different result, and don't invent an approval that didn't happen.”
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One shared hosted endpoint and a flat documented tool list. Some research tools internally run sub-agents, but that alone does not create a hierarchical MCP server.

E_aggregated.action_count: 24 documented active or separately referenced tool names
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official ZoomInfo-branded tool reference at https://gtm.ai/docs/mcp/tools names 26 tools, including Enrich Intent, Enrich News, and Enrich Scoops. Each deprecated tool page states that the hosted MCP server no longer exposes that tool, leaving 23 active names from that list. The FAQ separately names Submit Feedback as a tool; it is included as Official but absent from the 26-tool reference, so its default availability is Unknown. No catalogue-only tools were added. MartechDB describes the server's tools without machine names; AgentAtlas lists no additional native names; Claude connector directory is a third-party listing, not the source of this inventory.

E_aggregated.token_method: Public code of the server implementation and verbatim tools/list definitions or initialize instructions were unavailable. The official repository is a client plugin and skills package.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The vendor says MCP does not write to CRM, perform bulk exports, or run batch-enrichment pipelines; those workflows use the web app, REST API, CLI, or other integrations. Audience AI-column enrichment must be run in the ZoomInfo web app; MCP can define columns but the documented agent tool does not execute them. Sources: https://gtm.ai/docs/mcp/faq and https://gtm.ai/docs/mcp/tools/manage-audience-columns.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs recommend natural-language requests and automatic tool chaining. The credits page says the starter prompt asks for estimated cost and user approval before paid research; the server documentation does not establish that this confirmation is enforced. Tool pages advise passing exact search parameters to Upsert Audience and asking rather than guessing when audience intent is unclear.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Security page: “MCP doesn't grant access to any data beyond what your ZoomInfo package already includes.” It says tool calls run as the signed-in user, respect organization entitlements, and the server keeps no chat history between calls. It also says data passes through the AI provider, whose agreement governs retention and use, and recommends reviewing provider retention settings and turning off training where possible.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Docs state that ZoomInfo cannot see the rest of the AI conversation or context held by the AI client. The pricing page claims platform access is included at no extra cost and search/lookup are free. The FAQ says the product does not write to CRM or run bulk exports and batch enrichment pipelines.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Entitlement checks and per-user credit limits are described as enforced. The no-chat-history statement is a vendor claim without public server code for verification. Cost approval and tool-choice guidance are prompts/recommendations, not documented server-side enforcement. Pricing and workflow exclusions are documented product behavior; data handling promises are not independently verifiable from the public plugin repository.

contradictions: Official tool reference says it lists 26 tools, while three deprecated tool pages state those tools are no longer exposed; the FAQ separately references Submit Feedback, which is not in that 26-tool list.

The pre-fetched OAuth authorization-server metadata lists authorization_code and refresh_token grants, while ZoomInfo's OAuth guide also documents Client Credentials for service accounts. The metadata supplied does not list client_credentials in grant_types_supported.
The security documentation emphasizes sign-in by each user, while the OAuth guide describes a service-account Client Credentials option that runs calls as one shared integration identity.

Pricing page says Records Under Management is an Enterprise benefit and does not apply to Free, while the Credits & Billing page describes 12-month RUM treatment without that plan distinction. The pages may reflect different plan scopes or updated terms.
observations_for_research: The hosted server combines firmographic data access with organization-specific CRM and conversation context when connected; OAuth flow determines whether that context is user-specific or shared.
Client-side starter prompts recommend cost estimates and approval, while credit charging is based on tool operations and variable work, with no documented server-side pre-call cost preview.
Audience tools allow writes within ZoomInfo but intentionally leave some operations, including executing AI-column runs, to the web application.
notes: Reviewed links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and the local official repository. The official GTM AI documentation is branded “GTM AI by ZoomInfo” and identifies the same hosted endpoint. Public code reviewed is a plugin/skills bundle, not the server. All official tool reference sub-pages were checked; individual pages generally explain purpose and usage but do not publish machine input schemas. Pricing and legal pages were reviewed; legal pages were not used to infer MCP-specific retention beyond the security documentation. MartechDB and AgentAtlas were used as cross-checks only; the unofficial community server listed in links.json was excluded. actions.json contains 23 active names from the official list plus the FAQ's separately named Submit Feedback tool.
